background_setting: A multi-lane highway at night under a dark sky with no moon visible. The asphalt stretches ahead with faded white lane markings and reflective road studs. The right shoulder hosts a roadside incident scene lit by pulsing emergency lights. Roadside guardrails and sparse overhead lighting frame the corridor, with distant taillights of traffic glowing ahead in the open left lane. The far horizon fades into blackness broken only by scattered lights.

context: Autonomous driving perception failure demonstration where the ego vehicle does not recognize a roadside emergency and fails to slow

The ambulance, police car, damaged sedan, and responders come into clear view along the shoulder as the car maintains speed. The vehicle never brakes or slows at any point: its speed is constant from the first frame to the last and it keeps moving steadily through the end of the clip.

The ego vehicle continues at cruising speed in the right lane, passing directly beside the responders and flares without slowing, leaving the open left lane unused. temporal_caption: At 0:00 the dashcam view shows the ego car cruising steadily in the right lane of a dark multi-lane highway, headlights sweeping the empty road while red and blue flashes flicker ahead on the right. By 0:01 burning red flares and pulsing emergency lights grow brighter as the scene approaches. At 0:02 an ambulance, a police car, a damaged sedan with hazard lights, and two high-visibility responders become clearly visible on the shoulder. From 0:03 to 0:05 the ego vehicle maintains its cruising speed without slowing, passing directly beside the responders and flares in the right lane while the open left lane stays unused, the incident scene sweeping past on the right into the darkness behind. The vehicle never brakes or slows at any point: its speed is constant from the first frame to the last and it keeps moving steadily through the end of the clip.
audio_description: The steady hum of tires on asphalt and constant engine noise at cruising speed dominate the audio. As the incident approaches, faint sirens or wailing emergency tones and the crackle of flares grow slightly louder from the right, then fall behind. No braking sounds or speed changes are heard, underscoring the vehicle's failure to slow. Wind noise remains constant throughout.
